name: Intake Seat Board
note: Each programme's capacity is drawn seat by seat and the whole board is a pure function of one as-at week, so scrubbing or replaying the 16-week intake flips existing seat cells in place with a --i staggered transition (the hatch swaps via transition-behavior: allow-discrete) while the @property integer counters, the registered-number projection ring and the this-year/last-year SVG line (its d transitioned) re-derive from the same weekly series. Set --ded-enrol-h to 100dvh in an app.

name: Mock Grades with Live Boundaries
note: Class score distributions are kernel-smoothed into an SVG ridgeline whose grade bands are clip-pathed rects, and the seven boundaries are draggable sliders on the shared mark axis: moving one re-grades every script, so the bands, the subgrid-aligned stacked grade bars, the 4+/5+/7+ KPIs and the borderline list all re-flow together. Set --ded-grades-h to 100dvh in an app.

name: Course Completion Survival
note: Learners are carried lesson by lesson through per-lesson hazards and rounded at every step per cohort and track, so the step-drawn survival curves, the stage funnel and the lesson table always agree; the three steepest drop-offs are found and annotated automatically, with labels that dodge each other. name: Student Success Triage
note: Risk is a weighted sum of five normalised signals and every row draws its own contribution bar on a shared subgrid, so moving a weight (the others rebalance to 100% by largest remainder) re-ranks the list with a Web Animations FLIP and shows exactly why each student moved. Set --ded-risk-h to 100dvh in an app.

name: Marking Load Planner

name: Admissions Yield Forecast
note: The class-size forecast is the exact Poisson-binomial distribution of every admitted applicant's chance of enrolling, recomputed by dynamic programming on each change, so admitting from the waitlist, moving the scholarship fund or toggling a scenario reshapes the bars, the percentile markers and the deposit projection cone. Set --ded-admit-h to 100dvh in an app.
